newsitem.title: PERU: Peruvian navy finds presumed plane wreckage.
newsitem.headline: Peruvian navy finds presumed plane wreckage.

text.p: A search plane has found what is believed to be the wreckage of a Boeing 757-200 that crashed early Wednesday off Peru's Pacific Coast with 70 people on board, Peruvian navy officials said.
Admiral Cesar Chavez said a white fuselage, split in two, was spotted floating on the surface of the sea about 40 miles (60 km) west of the coast. There was no sign of survivors.
Chavez said that boats were heading for the zone to check the wreckage and search for more.
Officials at Peruvian airline Aeroperu, which owns the airplane, confirmed that it was carrying 61 passengers and nine crew members and suffered "technical faults" minutes before it crashed.
Aeroperu could not say if there were any survivors or give nationalities of the passengers.
But officials at Lima's Jorge Chavez international airport said at least 30 Chileans and one Briton were among the passengers.
